ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are three vertical straight lines ℓ, m, n, which are crossed by a transversal line t slanting from upper left to lower right. Near the intersection point of the right-side straight line n and the transversal line t are labeled angles 9, 10, 11, 12, among which ∠9 is at the upper left of the intersection point, and ∠12 is at the lower left of the intersection point. Reasoning: It is known that m∠9 = 75°. At this intersection point on straight line n, ∠9 and ∠12 are adjacent, sharing the side of transversal line t toward the left; their other two sides are respectively the upward and downward opposite rays on straight line n, so ∠9 and ∠12 form a linear pair, and their sum is 180°. Therefore m∠12 = 180° - 75° = 105°.

In the diagram, ∠9 and ∠12 are adjacent on the left side of line n, sharing one side along the transversal, while their other sides are opposite rays on the vertical line n. Therefore they form a linear pair, so m∠9 + m∠12 = 180. Compute m∠12 = 180 - 75 = 105.
